Title: Accept valid batch scope
Description: Verify that batch 5007 can be submitted as the run scope.
Preconditions: ABC implementation is deployed and batch 5007 is available.
Steps: 1. Open the batch execution interface. 2. Enter batch ID 5007. 3. Submit the run.
Expected Results: Batch ID 5007 is accepted and the run proceeds without a scope validation error.

Title: Reject an invalid batch scope
Description: Verify that a batch outside the requested scope cannot be executed as CSR-581.
Preconditions: The execution interface is available.
Steps: 1. Enter an invalid or unavailable batch ID such as 5008. 2. Submit the run.
Expected Results: The system rejects the invalid scope or reports that the batch is unavailable; no CSR-581 execution run is created.

Title: Create one execution run for the batch
Description: Verify that the accepted batch creates one traceable execution record.
Preconditions: Batch 5007 is available and no duplicate run is intentionally requested.
Steps: 1. Submit batch 5007 once. 2. Query the batch-run statistics for batch 5007. 3. Inspect the execution-run relationships.
Expected Results: One execution run is recorded for batch 5007 and its batch relationship is populated.

Title: Prevent accidental duplicate execution records
Description: Verify that repeated submission does not silently associate unrelated runs with the same execution.
Preconditions: Batch 5007 has an existing completed execution.
Steps: 1. Submit batch 5007 again without a new run request or idempotency key. 2. Query batch-run records.
Expected Results: The system applies its duplicate-run policy consistently; it does not overwrite the original execution identifiers or merge unrelated runs.

Title: Populate batch audit fields
Description: Verify all required batch-level fields are recorded.
Preconditions: A batch run for 5007 has completed.
Steps: 1. Query the batch-run record for batch 5007. 2. Inspect batch ID, execution run ID, source ID, instance ID, start time, end time, and status.
Expected Results: All required fields are present, associated with the same run, and contain valid values.

Title: Set batch completed after validation
Description: Verify that completed is assigned only after processing and validations finish.
Preconditions: Batch 5007 can be monitored during execution.
Steps: 1. Start batch 5007. 2. Observe the batch while child processing or validation is still active. 3. Query the final record after all work finishes.
Expected Results: The batch is not marked Completed while required work is active; after successful completion and validation its status is Completed.

Title: Confirm completed batch result
Description: Verify the QA baseline result for batch 5007.
Preconditions: The QA result data is loaded.
Steps: 1. Query batch-run statistics for batch 5007. 2. Compare the stored status with the QA result.
Expected Results: Batch 5007 has a recorded completed execution with populated start and end timestamps.

Title: Block batch success for failed child job
Description: Verify that a failed child job prevents a successful batch result.
Preconditions: A controllable test run can force job 50071 to fail.
Steps: 1. Start batch 5007 with job 50071 configured to fail. 2. Wait for child processing to finish. 3. Query the batch status.
Expected Results: The batch is not reported as successfully Completed; the child failure is retained and visible.

Title: Block batch success for incomplete child job
Description: Verify that an incomplete child job cannot be treated as a successful batch.
Preconditions: A controllable test run can leave job 50071 incomplete.
Steps: 1. Start batch 5007. 2. Stop or hold job 50071 before completion. 3. Query the batch status.
Expected Results: The batch remains non-successful or in progress according to the status policy and does not become Completed prematurely.

Title: Run configured job for batch 5007
Description: Verify that batch 5007 invokes job ID 50071.
Preconditions: Batch 5007 is accepted and the job configuration is deployed.
Steps: 1. Execute batch 5007. 2. Query job-run statistics for the resulting execution.
Expected Results: A job run for job ID 50071 is created under batch 5007.

Title: Preserve job-to-execution relationship
Description: Verify the job run retains its parent execution run ID.
Preconditions: A completed run for batch 5007 exists.
Steps: 1. Query job 50071. 2. Read its job run ID and execution run ID. 3. Compare the execution ID with the parent batch record.
Expected Results: The job run ID is populated and points to the execution run that belongs to batch 5007.

Title: Record configured job name
Description: Verify the job record identifies the configured GAA premium job.
Preconditions: Job 50071 has run.
Steps: 1. Query the job-run record. 2. Inspect the job name.
Expected Results: The job name identifies SDM_GAA_PREMIUM_PA_Extra... as represented in the QA evidence, with the full system value retained where available.

Title: Record Silver source
Description: Verify the job records Silver Delta Table as source system and path.
Preconditions: Job 50071 has run.
Steps: 1. Query the job-run record. 2. Inspect SourceSystem and SourcePath.
Expected Results: SourceSystem and SourcePath are recorded as Silver Delta Table.

Title: Record Backoffice target
Description: Verify the job records Backoffice Delta Table as target system and path.
Preconditions: Job 50071 has run.
Steps: 1. Query the job-run record. 2. Inspect TargetSystem and TargetPath.
Expected Results: TargetSystem and TargetPath are recorded as Backoffice Delta Table.

Title: Populate job timing and status
Description: Verify job start time end time and status are retained.
Preconditions: Job 50071 has completed.
Steps: 1. Query job-run statistics for job 50071. 2. Inspect JobStartTime JobEndTime and Status.
Expected Results: Both timestamps are populated in chronological order and the status is populated.

Title: Complete successful job
Description: Verify job 50071 is marked Completed after successful QA validation.
Preconditions: All required files reconcile for this controlled run.
Steps: 1. Run batch 5007 with valid source and target data. 2. Wait for validation to finish. 3. Query job status.
Expected Results: Job 50071 is marked Completed only after processing and validation finish successfully.

Title: Do not complete job with unresolved file validation
Description: Verify an unresolved file validation prevents a successful job status.
Preconditions: File 500718 has source count 1 and target count 3.
Steps: 1. Run batch 5007 using the QA baseline data. 2. Leave the 500718 mismatch unresolved. 3. Query the job status and file results.
Expected Results: The mismatch remains visible and the job is not treated as fully successful unless the agreed warning or exception policy explicitly allows completed-with-exception.

Title: Record all file metadata fields
Description: Verify every file record contains the complete metadata contract.
Preconditions: At least one source and one output file have been processed.
Steps: 1. Query file metadata for the execution. 2. Inspect file run ID execution run ID job run ID file ID file name timestamps duration source count target count and status.
Expected Results: Every required field is populated with the correct data type and the file run ID is unique.

Title: Link file records to batch
Description: Verify file records can be traced through execution and job relationships to batch 5007.
Preconditions: Batch 5007 and job 50071 have completed.
Steps: 1. Select a source file record. 2. Follow its job run ID to the execution run. 3. Follow the execution run to batch 5007.
Expected Results: The relationship chain resolves to batch 5007 without missing or conflicting identifiers.

Title: Record all source file IDs
Description: Verify source-side file IDs 500711 through 500718 are present.
Preconditions: The QA baseline run has completed.
Steps: 1. Query source-side file metadata for batch 5007. 2. Filter for file IDs 500711 through 500718.
Expected Results: All eight source-side file IDs are present and each has a corresponding name and count result.

Title: Record generated output files
Description: Verify premium driver and audit output records are present.
Preconditions: The output stage has completed.
Steps: 1. Query output-side file metadata. 2. Locate file IDs 500713 500714 and 500715. 3. Inspect names and statuses.
Expected Results: Premium driver and audit output records are present and distinguishable by file ID and file name.

Title: Populate file timestamps
Description: Verify each processed file has load start and end timestamps.
Preconditions: Source and output files have been processed.
Steps: 1. Query all file metadata records. 2. Check LoadStartTime and LoadEndTime for every record.
Expected Results: Every processed file has both timestamps and each end time is not earlier than its start time.

Title: Calculate file duration
Description: Verify duration in seconds agrees with recorded load timestamps.
Preconditions: File metadata includes timestamps and duration.
Steps: 1. Select each file record. 2. Calculate elapsed seconds from load start and end. 3. Compare with DurationInSeconds.
Expected Results: Recorded duration is non-negative and consistent with the timestamp precision and documented rounding policy.

Title: Keep file statuses independent
Description: Verify one file result cannot overwrite another file status.
Preconditions: The run contains at least two files with different validation outcomes.
Steps: 1. Process files 500717 and 500718. 2. Query both records after validation. 3. Compare their statuses and counts.
Expected Results: Each file retains its own status and counts; the 500718 exception does not change the reconciled result for 500717.

Title: Capture both count fields
Description: Verify source and target counts are stored for every file.
Preconditions: Files have been processed.
Steps: 1. Query source and output file metadata. 2. Inspect SourceCount and TargetCount for each record.
Expected Results: Both count fields are present for every record, including records with a mismatch.

Title: Pass equal counts
Description: Verify a file passes reconciliation when source and target counts are equal.
Preconditions: A test file has equal source and target counts.
Steps: 1. Process a file with source count 672 and target count 672. 2. Run file validation. 3. Inspect the result.
Expected Results: The file is classified as reconciled or passed and no count exception is raised.

Title: Detect target expansion
Description: Verify unequal counts do not pass reconciliation.
Preconditions: File 500718 is available with source count 1 and target count 3.
Steps: 1. Process file 500718. 2. Run count validation. 3. Inspect status and exception details.
Expected Results: The file fails or is flagged for exception because 1 does not equal 3; it is not classified as reconciled.

Title: Reconcile observed source counts
Description: Verify all observed equal source-side count pairs.
Preconditions: The QA baseline data is loaded.
Steps: 1. Validate file 500711 with 1768/1768. 2. Validate 500712 with 585/585. 3. Validate 500713 with 672/672. 4. Validate 500714 with 136/136. 5. Validate 500715 with 1/1. 6. Validate 500716 with 672/672. 7. Validate 500717 with 136/136.
Expected Results: All seven listed source-side records pass reconciliation with the exact observed counts.

Title: Reconcile observed output counts
Description: Verify all observed output count pairs pass.
Preconditions: The QA output records are available.
Steps: 1. Validate output 500713 with 672/672. 2. Validate output 500714 with 136/136. 3. Validate output 500715 with 1/1.
Expected Results: All three listed output records pass reconciliation with the exact observed counts.

Title: Record mismatch exception
Description: Verify a count mismatch creates a queryable validation exception.
Preconditions: File 500718 has source count 1 and target count 3.
Steps: 1. Run validation for file 500718. 2. Query the file result and exception details.
Expected Results: A validation exception is recorded with file ID 500718 and the result is not converted to pass by a completed batch.

Title: Preserve mismatch values
Description: Verify the actual 500718 counts remain visible.
Preconditions: File 500718 has been processed.
Steps: 1. Query metadata for 500718. 2. Read SourceCount and TargetCount.
Expected Results: SourceCount is 1 and TargetCount is 3; neither value is normalized or replaced by the other.

Title: Validate both source and output stages
Description: Verify count validation runs on source ingestion and generated output records.
Preconditions: Source and output records exist for the same execution.
Steps: 1. Run validation against source-side records. 2. Run validation against output-side records. 3. Compare validation results.
Expected Results: Both stages receive count validation and their results remain separately queryable.

Title: Identify discrepant file
Description: Verify the result directly identifies file 500718 as discrepant.
Preconditions: The QA baseline run has completed.
Steps: 1. Query file validation results. 2. Search for discrepant records. 3. Inspect the file ID.
Expected Results: File ID 500718 is included in the discrepancy results.

Title: Display exception counts
Description: Verify discrepancy details show actual source and target counts.
Preconditions: File 500718 has a recorded exception.
Steps: 1. Open the 500718 exception. 2. Inspect the displayed count values.
Expected Results: The exception displays SourceCount 1 and TargetCount 3.

Title: Trace exception to batch and job
Description: Verify an exception retains identifiers needed for investigation.
Preconditions: File 500718 belongs to batch 5007 and job 50071.
Steps: 1. Open the 500718 result. 2. Read its file run ID job run ID and execution run ID. 3. resolve the parent batch and job.
Expected Results: The exception can be traced to batch 5007 and job 50071 through retained identifiers.

Title: Preserve successful file results
Description: Verify a discrepant file does not obscure reconciled files.
Preconditions: The run includes reconciled file 500717 and discrepant file 500718.
Steps: 1. Query results after both files complete. 2. Inspect 500717 and 500718 independently.
Expected Results: The successful 500717 result remains available and reconciled while 500718 remains flagged.

Title: Expose file results separately from run status
Description: Verify consumers can inspect file-level results even when batch and job statuses are completed.
Preconditions: The QA baseline has completed batch and job statuses and a file mismatch.
Steps: 1. Query batch and job status. 2. Query file-level validation results. 3. Compare the two views.
Expected Results: Completed batch/job status does not conceal the 500718 file exception; both run-level and file-level results are available.

Title: Distinguish pass from investigation status
Description: Verify downstream consumers can separate reconciled files from files requiring investigation.
Preconditions: A reconciled file and 500718 exception are available.
Steps: 1. Query file records by status. 2. Compare the status and counts for 500717 and 500718.
Expected Results: The downstream consumer can classify 500717 as reconciled and 500718 as requiring investigation using stored status and counts.

Title: Generate premium output
Description: Verify the premium output for file 500713 is generated.
Preconditions: The GAA premium job is configured and source data is available.
Steps: 1. Run job 50071. 2. Locate the premium output record for file 500713. 3. Inspect its file name and existence.
Expected Results: A premium output file is generated and recorded under file ID 500713.

Title: Validate premium output count
Description: Verify premium output 500713 has counts 672 and 672.
Preconditions: Premium output 500713 has been generated.
Steps: 1. Query its source and target counts. 2. Run output validation.
Expected Results: File 500713 reports SourceCount 672 and TargetCount 672 and passes count reconciliation.

Title: Generate driver output
Description: Verify the driver output for file 500714 is generated.
Preconditions: The GAA premium job is configured and source data is available.
Steps: 1. Run job 50071. 2. Locate the driver output record for file 500714. 3. Inspect its file name and existence.
Expected Results: A driver output file is generated and recorded under file ID 500714.

Title: Validate driver output count
Description: Verify driver output 500714 has counts 136 and 136.
Preconditions: Driver output 500714 has been generated.
Steps: 1. Query its source and target counts. 2. Run output validation.
Expected Results: File 500714 reports SourceCount 136 and TargetCount 136 and passes count reconciliation.

Title: Generate audit output
Description: Verify the audit output for file 500715 is generated.
Preconditions: The GAA premium job is configured and source data is available.
Steps: 1. Run job 50071. 2. Locate the audit output record for file 500715. 3. Inspect its file name and existence.
Expected Results: An audit output file is generated and recorded under file ID 500715.

Title: Validate audit output count
Description: Verify audit output 500715 has counts 1 and 1.
Preconditions: Audit output 500715 has been generated.
Steps: 1. Query its source and target counts. 2. Run output validation.
Expected Results: File 500715 reports SourceCount 1 and TargetCount 1 and passes count reconciliation.

Title: Store output metadata and status
Description: Verify each generated output has an independent metadata record and status.
Preconditions: Premium driver and audit outputs have been generated.
Steps: 1. Query output metadata for 500713 500714 and 500715. 2. Inspect file identifiers metadata fields and statuses.
Expected Results: Each output has its own complete metadata record and processing status.

Title: Associate outputs with source run
Description: Verify output records use the same execution and job run as source processing.
Preconditions: Batch 5007 and job 50071 have generated outputs.
Steps: 1. Read execution and job run IDs on source records. 2. Read the same IDs on output records 500713 500714 and 500715. 3. Compare them.
Expected Results: Output records are linked to the same execution and job run as their source processing.

Title: Require output count comparison
Description: Verify an output cannot be marked validated before count comparison.
Preconditions: An output has been generated but validation has not run.
Steps: 1. Generate an output. 2. Inspect its status before validation. 3. Run count comparison. 4. Inspect status again.
Expected Results: The output is not validated before comparison; after equal counts are confirmed it can be marked reconciled or passed.

Title: Preserve execution parent
Description: Verify execution run is the parent of job run 50071.
Preconditions: Batch 5007 and job 50071 have completed.
Steps: 1. Query the execution record. 2. Query job run 50071. 3. Compare the job's parent execution run ID with the batch execution ID.
Expected Results: Job run 50071 points to the correct parent execution run.

Title: Preserve job parent for every file
Description: Verify every file run points to job run 50071.
Preconditions: File records for source and output files exist.
Steps: 1. Query all file runs for the execution. 2. Inspect each JobRunID. 3. Compare each value with 50071.
Expected Results: Every file run is linked to job run 50071 and no file is orphaned from the job.

Title: Trace every file to batch
Description: Verify each source and output result can be traced to batch 5007.
Preconditions: Batch 5007 has completed with source and output file records.
Steps: 1. Select each source and output file record. 2. Follow file run to job run and execution run. 3. Confirm the batch ID.
Expected Results: Every file result resolves to batch 5007 through the identifier chain.

Title: Retain all run timings
Description: Verify batch job and file start/end times remain available.
Preconditions: The full QA baseline run has completed.
Steps: 1. Query batch run timing. 2. Query job run timing. 3. Query file load timing. 4. Verify values after completion.
Expected Results: Batch job and file start/end timestamps are retained and chronologically valid.

Title: Query completed run results
Description: Verify statuses and count results remain queryable after completion.
Preconditions: Batch 5007 has completed and the result store is available.
Steps: 1. Query the batch after completion. 2. Query job 50071. 3. Query source and output file records and counts.
Expected Results: Completed statuses and all count results remain retrievable without rerunning the batch.

Title: Distinguish source and output records
Description: Verify audit data identifies source files separately from generated outputs.
Preconditions: Source and output records exist for the same run.
Steps: 1. Query all file metadata. 2. Group records by source or output role. 3. Inspect file IDs names and relationships.
Expected Results: Source-side records 500711 through 500718 are distinguishable from generated output records 500713 through 500715.

Title: Handle zero-count boundary
Description: Verify count validation handles a valid zero-to-zero file without treating zero as missing.
Preconditions: A controlled test file with source count 0 and target count 0 is available.
Steps: 1. Process the zero-record file. 2. Run count validation. 3. Inspect the result.
Expected Results: Both counts are recorded as numeric zero and the file passes equality validation; zero is not treated as null or absent.

Title: Handle missing count as exception
Description: Verify a missing source or target count cannot pass validation.
Preconditions: A controlled file record has one count omitted.
Steps: 1. Process the record with a missing count. 2. Run count validation. 3. Inspect status and exception.
Expected Results: The file is flagged as invalid or requiring investigation; missing data is not treated as an equal count.
